name: Prepare payroll from Gusto time data with Claude and approve in Slack

parameters.content:
## Prepare payroll from Gusto time data with Claude and approve in Slack

**Who's it for**
Small HR and finance teams that run payroll checks by hand every period and still find errors after the fact.

**How it works**
Trigger: Runs on the cut-off date each period, plus a preview run three days earlier so managers can fix missing approvals.
1. Collect period inputs
2. Normalise into one employee ledger
3. Validate against policy
4. Anomaly review
5. Send the exceptions report
6. Wait for approval
7. Push the run to the provider
8. Reconcile after the run
Every AI step is followed by a "Needs a person?" gate that parks low-confidence items instead of guessing, and the write-back waits for an approval in Slack or Gmail.

**How to set up**
1. Open "Config (edit me)" and fill in the fields (names, approver, quiet hours, thresholds).
2. Add credentials to each service node.
3. Run once with test_mode on, read the output, then switch the trigger on.

**Requirements**
An Anthropic API key for the Claude nodes, plus Gusto / ADP / Rippling / Deel, Slack, Google Sheets (or their equivalents — the nodes are standard and easy to swap).

**How to customize the workflow**
Set the pay-period rules and the anomaly thresholds in the Config node; connect Gusto, ADP, Rippling or Deel. Keep the guardrail: The workflow never submits without an explicit human approval; the Wait node is the control.

Full blueprint with trigger, steps, guardrails and where the standard version stops: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/payroll-automation/

## Payroll Automation Workflow

Starter template from agentmelt.com — configure before running:

1. Fill in "Config (edit me)" (name, approver, quiet hours; test_mode stays on for the first week).
2. Add credentials to every service node (Anthropic, mail, CRM, database…).
3. Replace placeholder URLs, queries and field mappings with yours.
4. Set the trigger: Runs on the cut-off date each period, plus a preview run three days earlier so managers can fix missing approvals.
5. Keep the gates: 'Needs a person?' after every AI step, 'Approved?' after the approval — wire their dead ends to a sheet or a channel.
6. Keep the guardrails:
   - The workflow never submits without an explicit human approval; the Wait node is the control.
   - The AI step annotates only; it has no write access to amounts.
   - Every submitted file is stored with a hash and the approver's identity for audit.
   - Provider totals are reconciled against the submitted ledger before payslips release.

Full blueprint and pricing: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/payroll-automation/
Want it built and run for you? $297/month · custom $4,000–6,000 one-time

## Steps

1. Schedule Trigger (daily)
2. HTTP Request: Collect period inputs
3. Code: Normalise into one employee ledger
4. IF: Validate against policy
5. AI Agent: Anomaly review
6. Slack: Send the exceptions report
7. Wait: Wait for approval
8. HTTP Request: Push the run to the provider
9. Compare Datasets: Reconcile after the run

Every AI step is followed by "Needs a person?"; the write-back waits for "Approved?" where the blueprint has an approval step.

Runs on the cut-off date each period, plus a preview run three days earlier so managers can fix missing approvals.

assignments.name: config.your_name
assignments.value: Your name — signs every outgoing message

assignments.name: config.approver
assignments.value: #approvals — a Slack channel, or an email address

nodes.name: Config (edit me)
nodes.notes:
Fill these in once; every later node reads them as $('Config (edit me)').item.json.config.*

test_mode = true: log what the workflow would write, without writing it, for the first week.
approval_mode = true: the approval node waits for a person; switch off per message type once it has earned it.

Also point the nodes at your own sources:
- Time tracking (Deputy, Clockify, Harvest, BambooHR Time)
- HRIS change log and leave balances
- Expense platform (Expensify, Ramp, Pleo)
- Payroll provider API (Gusto, ADP, Rippling, Deel, Xero)
- Policy rules sheet (limits, allowances, entity settings)

parameters.notes: Pulls approved hours from the time tracker (Deputy, Clockify, Harvest), leave from the HRIS, expense claims from Expensify or Ramp, and the change log (new hires, leavers, rate changes) from the HRIS.

nodes.name: HTTP Request: Collect period inputs
nodes.notes:
Collect period inputs

Pulls approved hours from the time tracker (Deputy, Clockify, Harvest), leave from the HRIS, expense claims from Expensify or Ramp, and the change log (new hires, leavers, rate changes) from the HRIS.

nodes.name: Code: Normalise into one employee ledger
nodes.notes:
Normalise into one employee ledger

One row per employee per period: base, hours, overtime, leave, allowances, deductions, one-offs. Currency and locale handled per entity.

nodes.name: IF: Validate against policy
nodes.notes:
Validate against policy

Deterministic rules: missing approvals, hours above contract limits, rate changes without an HRIS record, leavers with active pay, starters missing tax details. Each failure becomes an exception with the rule that fired.

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Anomaly review" step of the Payroll Automation Workflow workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: Compares each employee's line to their last six periods and explains outliers in one sentence with the evidence. It never changes a number — it annotates.

Rules:
- The workflow never submits without an explicit human approval; the Wait node is the control.
- The AI step annotates only; it has no write access to amounts.
- Every submitted file is stored with a hash and the approver's identity for audit.
- Provider totals are reconciled against the submitted ledger before payslips release.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.

nodes.name: AI Agent: Anomaly review
nodes.notes:
Anomaly review

Compares each employee's line to their last six periods and explains outliers in one sentence with the evidence. It never changes a number — it annotates.

nodes.name: Needs a person?
nodes.notes: True = the AI step was not sure or flagged the item → dead letter, a person looks. False = continue. Wire the dead letter to a Slack message or a sheet so nothing fails silently.

nodes.name: Needs a person: Anomaly review
nodes.notes: Dead letter. Replace this no-op with a Slack message or a sheet row that carries the raw item and the reason — silent failures are the ones that cost.

nodes.name: Slack: Send the exceptions report
nodes.notes:
Send the exceptions report

Payroll manager receives the ledger summary and the exceptions list with approve/hold buttons; managers get their team's missing approvals.

nodes.name: Wait: Wait for approval
nodes.notes:
Wait for approval

The workflow pauses until the payroll manager approves in Slack or the sheet. Nothing is sent to the provider without that click.

Compares the provider's processed totals to the submitted ledger and alerts on any difference before payslips go out.
